label: late copy-phase steps (last ~3 outputs), modulated by input token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (after <DEL>, 100% of mass). It never fires during the original tokens, at the delimiter step, or at the first copy step (recall_idx 0). It only fires on repeated inputs (in_first=0), which follows from being in the copy phase. It is concentrated near the end of the copy: to_go<=2 covers about 80% of activations and 84% of mass, but only 17% of those steps are active, so it is selective within that window. Which steps fire depends strongly on the input token: r, m, a, l, k, h (then d, v, i) have 2-4x lift. Restricting to those tokens raises precision to about 0.4 but drops mass recall to about 0.6, and no clean token set was found. Magnitude is largest for L=3 at the second copy step (e.g. a r b <DEL> a [r]) and is higher at later absolute steps (t 11-13, 17). No single coherent rule gets past F1 of about 0.48.
